## 2. Feature Description ✅<!--dv-evidence:-->

_Provenance: documented specification facts only; sources are linked from the heading indicator._


### Purpose

-  UART core provides serial communication with modem or other external devices using RS232 protocol. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Peer is modem or other external device over serial cable.
-  Core is designed for maximum compatibility with industry-standard National Semiconductors 16550A device. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Compatibility is at register level and functionality.
### Interface

-  Core provides WISHBONE slave interface for register access. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Interface is used for register access to UART.
-  Core provides modem control signals to a modem connected to the UART. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Control is performed through the modem control register.
-  Core provides optional BAUD_O output. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Output is optional.
### Mode

-  Core supports FIFO-only operation. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - No non-FIFO operation is supported.
-  In loopback mode the serial output STX_PAD_O is set to logic 1. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Transmitter shift register output is internally connected to receiver shift register input in loopback.
  - DTR connects to DSR, RTS to CTS, Out1 to RI, Out2 to DCD in loopback.
### Data Path

-  Upon reset the receiver and transmitter FIFOs are cleared. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Receiver and transmitter shift registers are also cleared on reset.
### Configuration

-  The two divisor latch bytes form one 16-bit register accessed internally as a single number. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Both bytes must be set to ensure normal operation.
-  Divisor latches are accessed by setting LCR bit 7 to 1. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Access to other registers at the same addresses is restored after clearing the bit.
-  Divisor value equals system clock speed divided by 16 times desired baud rate. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Setting uses system clock speed and desired baud rate.
### Limitation

-  Divisor latch reset value 0 disables all serial I/O operations. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Reset default requires explicit software setup before serial I/O.

### FIFO Control (FCR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 2 | Width: 8 | Access: W | Reset: 11000000b

#### Description

Control FIFO options

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Register selects FIFO trigger level threshold that enables the Received Data Available interrupt.
> Specification evidence: The FCR allows selection of the FIFO trigger level (the number of bytes in FIFO required
to enable the Received Data Available interrupt).

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | W | - | Ignored (Used to enable FIFOs in NS16550D). Since this UART only supports FIFO mode, this bit is ignored. | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 1 |  | W | - | Writing a ‘1’ to bit 1 clears the Receiver FIFO and resets its logic. But it doesn’t clear the shift register, i.e. receiving of the current character continues. | 1 = clears the Receiver FIFO and resets its logic. But it doesn’t clear the shift register, i.e. receiving of the current character continues. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 |  | W | - | Writing a ‘1’ to bit 2 clears the Transmitter FIFO and resets its logic. The shift register is not cleared, i.e. transmitting of the current character continues. | 1 = clears the Transmitter FIFO and resets its logic. The shift register is not cleared, i.e. transmitting of the current character continues. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5-3 |  | W | - | Ignored | - |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7-6 |  | W | - | Define the Receiver FIFO Interrupt trigger level | 00 = 1 byte; 01 = 4 bytes; 10 = 8 bytes; 11 = 14 bytes |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

<!--dv-register-detail:0966030f7f5930b2-->
### Interrupt Identification (IIR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 2 | Width: 8 | Access: R | Reset: C1h

#### Description

Get interrupt information

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Register reports highest priority pending interrupt status; it does not set modes, enables, masks, thresholds, timing, format or routing.
> Specification evidence: The IIR enables the programmer to retrieve what is the current highest priority pending
interrupt.

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Bit 0 | - | - | indicates that an interrupt is pending when it’s logic ‘0’; when it’s ‘1’ – no interrupt is pending. | 0 = an interrupt is pending; 1 = no interrupt is pending |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3-1 | Bit 3, Bit 2, Bit 1 | - | - | list of possible interrupts along with the bits they enable, priority, and their source and reset control. | 0 1 1 = 1st Receiver Line Status - Parity, Overrun or Framing errors or Break Interrupt; Interrupt Source: Parity, Overrun or Framing errors or Break Interrupt; Interrupt Reset Control: Reading the Line Status Register; 0 1 0 = 2nd Receiver Data available - FIFO trigger level reached; Interrupt Reset Control: FIFO drops below trigger level; 1 1 0 = 2nd Timeout Indication - There’s at least 1 character in the FIFO but no character has been input to the FIFO or read from it for the last 4 Char times; Interrupt Reset Control: Reading from the FIFO (Receiver Buffer Register); 0 0 1 = 3rd Transmitter Holding Register empty - Transmitter Holding Register Empty; Interrupt Reset Control: Writing to the Transmitter Holding Register or reading IIR; 0 0 0 = 4th Modem Status - CTS, DSR, RI or DCD; Interrupt Reset Control: Reading the Modem status register |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5-4 | Bits 4 and 5 | - | - | Logic ‘0’. | 0 = Logic ‘0’. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7-6 | Bits 6 and 7 | - | - | Logic ‘1’ for compatibility reason. | 1 = Logic ‘1’ for compatibility reason. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

<!--dv-register-detail:46c60da3fc4c938d-->
### Line Control Register (LCR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 3 | Width: 8 | Access: RW | Reset: 00000011b

#### Description

Control connection

Configuration identification  📄<!--dv-sources:--> NEEDS_REVIEW: Register controls line control parameters including data bits, parity and stop bits, which is format configuration.
> Specification evidence: Set the Line Control Register to the desired line control parameters.

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-0 | Select number of bits in each character | RW | - | Select number of bits in each character | 00 = 5 bits; 01 = 6 bits; 10 = 7 bits; 11 = 8 bits |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 | Specify the number of generated stop bits | RW | - | Specify the number of generated stop bits. Note that the receiver always checks the first stop bit only. | 0 = 1 stop bit; 1 = 1.5 stop bits when 5-bit character length selected and 2 bits otherwise |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3 | Parity Enable | RW | - | Parity Enable | 0 = No parity; 1 = Parity bit is generated on each outgoing character and is checked on each incoming one. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 4 | Even Parity select | RW | - | Even Parity select | 0 = Odd number of ‘1’ is transmitted and checked in each word (data and parity combined). In other words, if the data has an even number of ‘1’ in it, then the parity bit is ‘1’.; 1 = Even number of ‘1’ is transmitted in each word. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5 | Stick Parity bit. | RW | - | Stick Parity bit. | 0 = Stick Parity disabled; 1 = If bits 3 and 4 are logic ‘1’, the parity bit is transmitted and checked as logic ‘0’. If bit 3 is ‘1’ and bit 4 is ‘0’ then the parity bit is transmitted and checked as ‘1’. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 6 | Break Control bit | RW | - | Break Control bit | 1 = the serial out is forced into logic ‘0’ (break state).; 0 = break is disabled |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 7 | Divisor Latch Access bit. | RW | - | Divisor Latch Access bit. | 1 = The divisor latches can be accessed; 0 = The normal registers are accessed |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

<!--dv-register-detail-end-->

<!--dv-register-detail:2bf969f290793688-->
### Modem Control (MCR)  📄<!--dv-sources:-->
Address: 4 | Width: 8 | Access: W | Reset: 0

Status information

Status
Register

#### Fields

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Data Ready (DR) | R | - | Data Ready (DR) indicator. '0' - No characters in the FIFO. '1' - At least one character has been received and is in the FIFO. | 0 = No characters in the FIFO; 1 = At least one character has been received and is in the FIFO. |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 1 | Overrun Error (OE) | R | - | Overrun Error (OE) indicator. '1' - FIFO full and another character received in receiver shift register; bit cleared upon reading; generates Receiver Line Status interrupt. '0' - No overrun state. | 1 = If the FIFO is full and another character has been received in the receiver shift register. If another character is starting to arrive, it will overwrite the data in the shift register but the FIFO will remain intact. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No overrun state |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 2 | Parity Error (PE) | R | - | Parity Error (PE) indicator. '1' - Character at top of FIFO received with parity error; bit cleared upon reading; generates Receiver Line Status interrupt. '0' - No parity error in current character. | 1 = The character that is currently at the top of the FIFO has been received with parity error. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No parity error in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 3 | Framing Error (FE) | R | - | Framing Error (FE) indicator. '1' - Received character at top of FIFO did not have valid stop bit; bit cleared upon reading; generates Receiver Line Status interrupt. '0' - No framing error in current character. | 1 = The received character at the top of the FIFO did not have a valid stop bit. Of course, generally, it might be that all the following data is corrupt. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No framing error in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 4 | Break Interrupt (BI) | R | - | Break Interrupt (BI) indicator. '1' - Break condition reached in current character; bit cleared upon reading; generates Receiver Line Status interrupt. '0' - No break condition in current character. | 1 = A break condition has been reached in the current character. The break occurs when the line is held in logic 0 for a time of one character (start bit + data + parity + stop bit). In that case, one zero character enters the FIFO and the UART waits for a valid start bit to receive next character. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.; 0 = No break condition in the current character |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 5 | Transmit FIFO is empty | R | - | Transmit FIFO is empty. '1' - Transmitter FIFO is empty; generates Transmitter Holding Register Empty interrupt; cleared when data is written to transmitter FIFO. '0' - Otherwise. | 1 = The transmitter FIFO is empty. Generates Transmitter Holding Register Empty interrupt. The bit is cleared when data is being been written to the transmitter FIFO.; 0 = Otherwise |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |
| 6 | Transmitter Empty | R | - | Transmitter Empty indicator. '1' - Both the transmitter FIFO and transmitter shift register [description truncated in chunk]. | 1 = Both the transmitter FIFO and transmitter shift register |  📄<!--dv-sources:--> |

### RTLOBS-4bc43f4fc4 — reset ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Software FIFO resets rx_reset/tx_reset appear as single-cycle self-clearing pulses: loaded from FCR write data only when wb_we and wb_addr match FCR, otherwise forced to 0, with leading wb_rst_i branch forcing 0. Graph infers posedge clk clocking and wb_rst_i control dependence; reset role is candidate and needs review.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from the full always block showing wb_rst_i branch forcing both resets to 0, FCR-write branch loading wb_dat_i bits, and else branch forcing 0, plus individual assign excerpts for each branch; graph also infers posedge clk clocking and wb_rst_i control dependence.
- **Proposed test:** Test FCR write with bit1/bit2 set/clear and check rx_reset/tx_reset pulse width in clocks, auto-clear without re-write, separate vs simultaneous assertion, and behavior when wb_rst_i asserts during/after FCR write.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Confirm that rx_reset/tx_reset are intended as single-cycle auto-clearing pulses loaded from wb_dat_i[1]/[2] only on FCR writes, and confirm precedence when wb_rst_i asserts in the same cycle as a FCR write or back-to-back FCR writes?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (8 excerpts)
  - lines 500-513
  - lines 501
  - lines 503
  - lines 504
  - lines 508
  - lines 509
  - lines 511
  - lines 512

### RTLOBS-2899adbeb1 — dependency ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Global enable is generated from divisor-latch-related condition |dl and not |dlc with async wb_rst_i clear, and the same net fans out to both receiver.enable and transmitter.enable. Retrieved spec mentions divisor/baud relation and init but not this gating implementation.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from enable flop excerpt showing async wb_rst_i clear and next-state conditioned on |dl and ~(|dlc), combined with instantiation excerpts that pass the same enable net to both receiver and transmitter ports aliased to regs enable.
- **Proposed test:** Sweep divisor-latch values including 0 and dlc transitions, check enable assertion/deassertion latency, and check that Tx and Rx stall/enable together versus spec initialization sequence.
- **Specification comparison:** NOT_FOUND_IN_RETRIEVED_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Is enable intended to gate both transmitter and receiver together based on divisor-latch state |dl and dlc, and what are dl/dlc definitions and required programming sequence to enable/disable traffic?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (4 excerpts)
  - lines 379
  - lines 399-400
  - lines 704-713
  - lines 706

### RTLOBS-baca091327 — integration ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Modem inputs show continuous assignment driving {cts_pad_i, dsr_pad_i, ri_pad_i, dcd_pad_i} from internal modem_inputs. Spec lists those pads as Input direction, so internal driving versus boundary input needs clarification for integration and possible contention.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Inference:** Derived from continuous-assign excerpt that places pad_i-labeled nets on the left-hand side driven by modem_inputs vector, while graph records reads of modem_inputs and writes to each pad_i net in the same process.
- **Proposed test:** Check uart_top boundary connectivity for modem pads vs internal modem_inputs driver, test for multiple drivers/contention, and verify modem-status change detection under asynchronous pad toggles.
- **Specification comparison:** POSSIBLE_CONFLICT (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Are cts/dsr/ri/dcd_pad_i top-level inputs or internally driven loopback/debug nets, and where does modem_inputs originate and how is it synchronized/sampled for MSR?
- **RTL sources:** rtl/verilog/uart_regs.v (1 excerpt)
  - lines 341

### RTLOBS-4a0312555c — feature ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Internal msi_reset shows self-dependent pulse behavior with multiple set-to-1 branches and a clear-to-0 branch under if(msi_reset) for Modem Status Register reset. Retrieved excerpts do not detail this pulse duration or bit coverage.

- **Proposed test:** Trigger the msi_reset generation path, measure pulse width and which MSR delta/status bits clear, and test interaction with concurrent MSR read and wb_rst_i.

- **Designer question:** What event sets msi_reset to 1, how many clocks does it stay at 1 given the if(msi_reset) self-clear path, and which Modem Status Register bits does it clear?

### RTLOBS-212eb6cca2 — reset ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Reset uses two tiers: global wb_rst_i distributed to regs, transmitter, receiver and both FIFOs, plus separate software fifo_reset tx_reset to TX FIFO and rx_reset to RX FIFO. Graph infers async-high role from leading branches; sequencing of global versus software resets is candidate handling to verify alongside spec reset clearing.

### RTLOBS-bde785f7e0 — dependency ⚠️<!--dv-evidence:-->

Receiver status forms a three-level alias chain: fifo_rx overrun/push to receiver rf_overrun/rf_push_pulse to regs rf_overrun/rf_push_pulse. Spec documents overrun as line-status interrupt source, but multi-level propagation and clear interaction are implementation handling to test.

**Review:** NEEDS_REVIEW — RTL design engineer

- **Proposed test:** Fill RX FIFO to overrun, check overrun assertion path and LSR/IIR indication, then test clearing via LSR read versus rx_reset/wb_rst_i and check push-pulse loss under back-to-back receives.
- **Specification comparison:** DOCUMENTED_IN_SPEC (gap/conflict unconfirmed)
- **Designer question:** Confirm overrun/push-pulse propagation latency and persistence from fifo_rx through receiver to regs, and how overrun is cleared relative to LSR read versus FIFO reset?

## 12. Assumptions

_Provenance: unmarked facts are documented; ⚠️ marks inference and 🛑 marks assumed or unreferenced content. Heading links collect documented sources. 📄 hovers source excerpts._


### Assumption

- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume system CLK is stable and free-running before wishbone_reset_agent deasserts WB_RST_I and init_config_sequence starts. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - System clock is the WISHBONE bus clock source for baud derivation.
  - Reuse system_clock_agent clock_generate with chip_reset_sequence to guarantee stable clocks before traffic.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume WB_RST_I is asynchronous and held long enough by reset_drive to clear FIFOs and shift registers before register access. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Covers receiver and transmitter FIFOs plus shift registers cleared on reset.
  - Reuse wishbone_reset_agent reset_drive with chip_reset_sequence before wishbone_register_access.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume 8-bit WISHBONE slave accesses use WB_ADDR_I, WB_SEL_I, WB_DAT_I and WB_DAT_O with single WB_ACK_O per transfer. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - DUT acts as responder on wishbone_slave_interface.
  - Reuse wishbone_slave_interface_agent with wishbone_register_access for register traffic.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume UART operates FIFO-only with no non-FIFO mode available for verification. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - No bypass or character-mode checking is planned.
  - Reuse uart_serial_data_agent with uart_frame_traffic for FIFO data-path traffic.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume post-reset line format is 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit until LCR is reprogrammed. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Covers STX_PAD_O transmit and SRX_PAD_I receive framing in uart_serial_data_agent.
  - Line parameters are changed only through LCR programming in init_config_sequence.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume divisor value follows input clock divided by 16 times baud rate and zero keeps serial I/O stalled. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Divisor latches are accessed with LCR bit 7 control in init_config_sequence.
  - Zero divisor is assumed to stall transmitter and receiver traffic.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume INT_O remains asserted until the highest-priority pending source is serviced through IIR, LSR or MSR reads. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - DUT sources single INT_O observed by interrupt_output_agent with interrupt_observe.
  - All interrupts are assumed disabled after reset until IER is programmed.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume optional BAUD_O 16x tick is observed only when bonded and otherwise excluded from block checks. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Treated as observed_output when present in baud_rate_output group.
  - No driving or functional dependency is assumed for WISHBONE or serial traffic.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume FIFO trigger level defaults to 14 bytes in init_config_sequence unless a test overrides it. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Higher trigger is assumed to reduce interrupt frequency to the system.
  - Reuse wishbone_register_access to program trigger before enabling interrupts.
- 🛑<!--dv-evidence:--> Assume modem handshake inputs are asynchronous external toggles sampled for status reporting and loopback routing. 📄<!--dv-sources:-->
  - Covers RTS_PAD_O and DTR_PAD_O drives and CTS, DSR, RI, DCD sampling in modem_control_agent.
  - Reuse modem_handshake_toggle with loopback_traffic_sequence for integration.

### Reference CH-0174a058ac

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.15

> 4.8 Modem Status Register (MSR)
> 
> The register displays the current state of the modem control lines. Also, four bits also
> provide an indication in the state of one of the modem status lines. These bits are set to
> ‘1’ when a change in corresponding line has been detected and they are reset when the
> register is being read.
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 R Delta Clear To Send (DCTS) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The CTS line has changed its state.
> 1 R Delta Data Set Ready (DDSR) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The DSR line has changed its state.
> 2 R Trailing Edge of Ring Indicator  (TERI) detector. The RI line has
> changed its state from low to high state.
> 3 R Delta Data Carrier De tect (DDCD) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The DCD line has changed its state.
> 4 R Complement of the CTS input or equals to RTS in loopback mode.
> 5 R Complement of the DSR input or equals to DTR in loopback mode.
> 6 R Complement of the RI input or equals to Out1 in loopback mode.
> 7 R Complement of the DCD input or equals to Out2 in loopback mode.

### Reference CH-06bad6ffcd

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.15

> 4.9 Divisor Latches
> 
> The divisor latches can be accessed by setting the 7th bit of LCR to ‘1’. You should
> restore this bit to ‘0’ after setting the divisor latches in order to restore access to the other
> registers that occupy the same addresses. The 2 bytes form one 16-bit register, which is
> internally accessed as a single number. You should therefore set all 2 bytes of the register
> to ensure normal operation. The register is set to the default value of 0 on reset, which
> disables all serial I/O operations in order to ensure explicit setup of the register in the
> software. The value set should be equal to (system clock speed) / (16 x desired baud rate).
> The internal counter starts to work when the LSB of DL is written, so when setting the
> divisor, write the MSB first and the LSB last.
> 

### Reference CH-1e2324cfc3

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.17

> 5.1 Initialization
> 
> Upon reset the core performs the following tasks:
> 
> • The receiver and transmitter FIFOs are cleared.
> • The receiver and transmitter shift registers are cleared
> • The Divisor Latch register is set to 0.
> • The Line Control Register is set to communication of 8 bits of data, no parity, 1
> stop bit.
> • All interrupts are disabled in the Interrupt Enable Register.
> 
> For proper operation, perform the following:
> 
> • Set the Line Control Register to the desired line control parameters. Set bit 7 to ‘1’
> to allow access to the Divisor Latches.
> • Set the Divisor Latches, MSB first, LSB next.
> • Set bit 7 of LCR to ‘0’ to disable access to Divisor Latches. At this time the
> transmission engine starts working and data can be sent and received.
> • Set the FIFO trigger level. Generally, higher trigger level values produce less
> interrupt to the system, so setting it to 14 bytes is recommended if the system

> 1
> Introduction

> The UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) core provides serial
> communication capabilities, which allow communication with modem or other external

> designed to be maximally compatible with the industry standard National
> Semiconductors’ 16550A device.
>

>

> • FIFO only operation
> • Register level and functionality compatibility with NS16550A (but not 16450).

### Reference CH-419b99d7d8

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.17

> 5
> Operation
> 
> This UART core is very similar in operation to the standard 16550 UART chip with the
> main exception being that only the FIFO mode is supported. The scratch register is
> removed, as it serves no purpose.
> 
> This core can operate in 8-bit data bus mode or in 32-bit bus mode, which is now the
> default mode.
> 
> The 32-bit mode is fully WISHBONE compatible and it uses the WISHBONE [SEL_I]
> signal to properly receive and return 8-bit data on 32-bit data bus. The 8-bit version might
> have problems in various WISHBONE implementations because a 32-bit master reading
> from 8-bit bus can expect data on different bytes of the 4-byte word, depending on the
> register address.
> Also, in 32-bit data bus mode, the [ADR_I] is 5 and not 3 bits wide.
> 
> In addition, in the 32-bit data bus mode a debug interface is present in the system. This
> interface has 2 32-bit registers that can be read to provide non-intrusive look into the
> core’s registers and other internal values of importance.

### Reference CH-a2dd758e55

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.14

> 4.7 Line Status Register (LSR)
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 R Data Ready (DR) indicator.
>  ‘0’ – No characters in the FIFO
>  ‘1’ – At least one character has been received and is in the
> FIFO.
> 1 R Overrun Error (OE) indicator
>  ‘1’ – If the FIFO is full and another character has been
> received in the receiver shift register. If another character is starting
> to arrive, it will overwrite the data in the shift register but the FIFO
> will remain intact. The bit is cleared upon reading from the register.
> Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.
>  ‘0’ – No overrun state
> 2 R Parity Error (PE) indicator
>  ‘1’ – The character that is currently at the top of the FIFO
> has been received with parity error. The bit is cleared upon reading
> from the register. Generates Receiver Line Status interrupt.
>  ‘0’ – No parity error in the current character
> 3 R Framing Error (FE) indicator

>  ‘0’ – 1 stop bit
>  ‘1’ – 1.5 stop bits when 5-bit character length selected and
>   2 bits otherwise
>

### Reference CH-dfb1048908

Source: uart16550/doc/UART_spec.pdf, p.11

> 4.4 FIFO Control Register (FCR)
> 
> The FCR allows selection of the FIFO trigger level (the number of bytes in FIFO required
> to enable the Received Data Available interrupt).  In addition, the FIFOs can be cleared
> using this register.
> 
> Bit # Access Description
> 0 W Ignored (Used to enable FIFOs in NS16550D). Since this UART
> only supports FIFO mode, this bit is ignored.
> 1 W Writing a ‘1’ to bit 1 clears the Receiver FIFO and resets its logic.
> But it doesn’t clear the shift register, i.e. receiving of the current
> character continues.
> 2 W Writing a ‘1’ to bit 2 clears the Transmitter FIFO and resets its
> logic. The shift register is not cleared, i.e. transmitting of the
> current character continues.
> 5-3 W Ignored
> 7-6 W Define the Receiver FIFO Interrupt trigger level
>  ‘00’ – 1 byte
>  ‘01’ – 4 bytes
>  ‘10’ – 8 bytes
